title: Tip from Angela - Retrieval is How You Learn
summary: A study tip: following tutorials feels easy, but solving problems alone is a different skill. Regular retrieval practice closes that gap.

concepts.heading: Key takeaways
points: Feeling that everything makes sense while watching, then blanking on a challenge, is common and expected around this stage of the course.
Watching recognises information; coding requires recalling it from memory. They are separate skills, so passive viewing alone does not build the second.
Practise retrieval often: find extra exercises online, write your own quizzes, and try variations of what a lesson showed.
Predict the next step: pause before the instructor demonstrates something and attempt it yourself first.
More active practice leads to a firmer grasp than extra listening.

pitfalls: Binge-watching lectures without attempting the exercise first.

gaps_and_ideas: (Extra) Possible 'pause and predict' prompt or self-quiz feature on lesson pages.
